data: How was the F1-score calculated, and how does it influence the results?

The F1-score is a measure of a model's performance, combining precision and recall into a single score. It is calculated as 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall). The higher the F1-score, the better the model performs. In this case, the F1-scores for different models (CNN-char, SCAP, CNN-word-word-char, and CNN-word-char) are shown across two datasets: Emails and Blogs. The lines represent the F1-scores of these models as the number of authors increases. The color-coding helps distinguish between the models. The relationship between the models' performances can be observed through their respective line trends.
